summary: Sonam Gyatso is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1960–1970) and was a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Jamtsho works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a doctoral local researcher at the University of Hamburg, where he was also attested as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter in 2026.

Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (2006–2015) under Dan Arnold. In 2022, he became an assistant professor at Yale University.

Sonam Kinga is a historian and Tibetologist who studied at Sherubtse College (~1994–1998) and earned a PhD from Kyoto University (2007–2010). He was a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (~1999–2007) and a fellow at Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (2026).
Sonam Thakchoe works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tasmania (1999–2002) and became a senior philosophy lecturer there in 2003.

Sonam Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral research under Gray Tuttle. He serves at Columbia University as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program (attested 2026).
Sondra L. Hausner specializes in religious studies and Indology. She is attested in 2026 as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at both the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Songeun Choe specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Myung-dae Moon and pursued doctoral research under Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonika Gupta specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1993–1997) and was appointed professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras in 2025.

Sonja Arntzen specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her BA (1962–1966) and PhD (1970–1979) at the University of British Columbia, where Leon Hurvitz was her doctoral supervisor.

Sonja Glauch is a linguist who completed her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she became Akademische Oberrätin in 2007. She also held visiting professorships at the University of Vienna (2008) and University of Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and art history. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under Hung Wu (attested 2004) and has held posts at Swarthmore College, Stanford University, and the University of Southern California.

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil from the University of Oxford (1998–2003) under Richard Gombrich, becoming a professor at Dongguk University in 2004.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the National University of Singapore under Saranindranath Tagore and was attested as a visiting professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Sophus Bugge was a Norwegian linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, University of Copenhagen, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held positions at the University of Oslo beginning in 1860, including lektor in 1866, and also taught at Uppsala University.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 2000, 2015).

Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and Koyasan University, earning a doctorate in Esoteric Buddhism (~2008–2013), and held research posts at Koyasan University and a lectureship at Sonoda Women's University.

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor and dean (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soumyajit Sen is an Indologist who completed a BA at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira and a PhD at Jadavpur University (2016–2022). He became an assistant professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Keio University and trained under Kōsen Imakita and Ekkei Shuken. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
